answer: Temporal Ridge Admission. Each agent must publish its first N messages on a fixed cadence; the platform tracks inter-message timing and plots it as a drift profile, admitting only identities whose profile stays within a narrow ridge around the median curve. Duplicates spun up in bulk inherit near-identical cadences, so honest newcomers must instead spend real wall-clock time ramping along a spiral of gradually tightening intervals. To fake K identities an attacker must run K parallel timing schedules with deliberate jitter and random willow-like branching delays,
